summary: Configured a persistent ufw firewall on node1: SSH (22/tcp) allowed from anywhere, 9000/tcp allowed only from node2 (10.100.49.11), and 9000/tcp rejected from all other sources (verified against node3). ufw is enabled at boot via systemd. Also ran the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all three nodes, restarting one at a time, confirming changed boot identity, and re-verifying firewall behavior after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 24.04) and available firewall tooling; ufw present and systemd-enabled
Set ufw default deny incoming / allow outgoing on node1
Added rule: allow 9000/tcp from node2 (10.100.49.11) only
Added rule: reject 9000/tcp from anywhere (catches node3 and all other sources due to rule ordering)
Enabled ufw persistently (active + enabled on startup)
Functionally verified with a live nc listener on node1:9000: node2 connects successfully, node3 gets connection refused, SSH reachable from both
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all three nodes plus ufw rule state on node1
Restarted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, re-verified ufw rules and live functional test (node2 allowed, node3 rejected) post-reboot
Restarted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, re-verified node2->node1:9000 still succeeds
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, re-verified node3->node1:9000 still rejected and SSH still reachable
Cleaned up temporary nc listeners used for testing

evidence.requirement: Persistent host firewall configured on node1 (SSH open, port 9000 scoped to node2 only, rejected elsewhere)
evidence.summary: ufw enabled with default deny incoming; rule set shows 22/tcp allow anywhere, 9000/tcp allow only from 10.100.49.11 (node2), 9000/tcp reject from anywhere else, for both IPv4 and IPv6, with firewall reported active and enabled on startup

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: node2 can reach 9000, node3 and general traffic are rejected, SSH remains open to all
evidence.summary: Live nc listener on node1:9000; node2 nc -zv succeeded on 9000 and 22; node3 nc -zv on 9000 returned connection refused while 22 succeeded

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on node1 (boot id + firewall state)
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id c0691b74... and full active ufw ruleset before restart

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on node2 and node3 (boot id)
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id 17b362d1... and node3 boot_id b19a635d... before their restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent polls failed (unreachable) then succeeded with new boot_id 0f65abd0...; ufw ruleset confirmed intact post-reboot; live functional retest showed node2 allowed and node3 rejected on port 9000, matching pre-restart behavior

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; polls failed then succeeded with new boot_id 7e640741...; node2->node1:9000 connectivity re-verified successful after node2's own restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; polls failed then succeeded with new boot_id 960a28a3... (was b19a635d...); post-reboot test confirmed node3->node1:9000 still rejected and SSH still reachable, matching required firewall policy

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts, final firewall state confirmation
evidence.summary: Test nc listener killed on node1; final ufw status verbose shows the same persistent rule set active after all three node restarts
